assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: The response provides Table 1 (Reis Discount Tier for adults/seniors), Table 2 (Child Flat Discount), and Table 3 (Final ticket price arithmetic). While discount ladder and traveller eligibility are separated, no dedicated table tests rolling window boundary conditions (e.g., a ticket at exactly 30 days vs 31 days). The response mentions the 30-day window in the text but contains no structured test cases for the boundary.

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented — either as a row in the eligibility table or a separate note. It does not follow the ladder.
assertions.evidence: Table 2 — Child Flat Discount states: 'Children always receive a flat 20% regardless of how many tickets they have purchased.' The table demonstrates this with two scenarios, both yielding 20%, independent of the tier ladder in Table 1.

assertions.text: The discount ladder has multiple tiers derived from the 'every fifth trip' rule, with boundary values or value sets showing which ticket counts produce which discount. The maximum 40% discount is represented.
assertions.evidence: The tier boundaries table shows: '0 – 3 | 0%, 4 – 8 | 5%, 9 – 13 | 10%, 14 – 18 | 15%, 19 – 23 | 20%, 24 – 28 | 25%, 29 – 33 | 30%, 34 – 38 | 35%, 39 + | 40%'. The central rule text explains 'discount is determined by how many single tickets the passenger has purchased in the last 30 days,' and the boundaries follow the 5-ticket intervals ('Fifth ticket — first discount applies', 'Tenth ticket — second tier begins').

assertions.text: The 30-day rolling window boundary is tested: a ticket at exactly 30 days is included, at 31 days is excluded.
assertions.evidence: While the response discusses the 30-day rolling window ('discount is determined by how many single tickets the passenger has purchased in the last 30 days'), the scenario table shows various ticket counts but does NOT include explicit test cases comparing a ticket at exactly 30 days versus 31 days to verify boundary inclusion/exclusion behavior.

assertions.text: Eligibility uses human-readable values (yes/no or equivalent) rather than raw true/false. TypeConverter or similar mechanism mentioned.
assertions.evidence: The response uses human-readable values (Adult, Senior, Child, discount percentages like '5%' instead of 0.05). However, 'TypeConverter or similar mechanism' is not mentioned anywhere in the response, neither in the table descriptions nor in the open questions section.

assertions.text: Value sets in the tier table contain exactly the values that produce the same discount. No cross-tier contamination.
assertions.evidence: The tier boundaries table segments the ticket count ranges cleanly: '0 – 3', '4 – 8', '9 – 13', '14 – 18', '19 – 23', '24 – 28', '29 – 33', '34 – 38', '39 +'. Each range maps to a unique discount percentage with no overlaps, ensuring no values appear in multiple tiers.

assertions.text: The discount ladder table uses value sets for the ticket count column to group counts within the same tier (e.g. {5, 6, 7, 8, 9} or {5, 9} for min/max → 5%) — not one row per boundary value. The 'every fifth trip' rule creates tiers; the table should express tiers, not enumerate boundaries.
assertions.evidence: The tier boundaries table uses range notation (e.g., '4 – 8', '9 – 13') rather than explicit value set notation like '{4, 5, 6, 7, 8}' or '{4, 9}' as specified in the assertion. Although ranges avoid enumerating per-value rows, the format does not match the required value set representation.

assertions.text: The tier-to-discount mapping is expressed once — not repeated across multiple tables. A price application table (if present) should test the arithmetic (base price × discount → final price) without re-enumerating which ticket counts map to which tier.
assertions.evidence: Table 1 and its derived tier boundaries table express the ticket-count-to-discount mapping once. Table 3 (Final ticket price) tests arithmetic using discount percentages ('0%', '5%', '40%', '20%') directly without re-mapping ticket counts to tiers, only showing base price × discount → final price calculations.
